title: Frank Brangwyn: Color and Tone
content: Frank Brangwyn(Anglo-Welsh 1867-1956) typically worked with a relatively limited palette that included flake white, yellow ochre, raw sienna, burnt sienna, cadmium red, Venetian red, vermilion, and French blue.Frank Brangwyn, Market Scene Jaffa, 189050.5 x 61cm (19 7/8 x 24in).BiographerWalter Shaw-Sparrowsaid, "The thing that counted as the saving grace of style wastone,which may be described as a unifying mystery of colour that permeates a picture, and binds all its parts together, giving a sort of inner depth and richness....Nature is a vast unity with scattered parts, while art is a limited harmony; and it is tone that helps us to resolve profusion into a definite whole, true to the same key in every plot of colour."---FromFrank Brangwyn and His Work by Walter Shaw-Sparrow,1915.
